title: SEC-TESTS: bt5.6 signing key wrong-length has no test
description: The fix for bt5.6 added length validation in load_or_generate_signing_key() (reader/src/store/server_stores.rs lines 205-213): it now returns Err if the signing key file does not contain exactly 32 bytes. There is no #[test] covering this error path. The function is private (fn load_or_generate_signing_key) but the behavior is observable via ServerStores::from_config() which is public. A test must: write a tempfile with 31 bytes, call load_or_generate_signing_key (or ServerStores::from_config() with a path pointing to the tempfile), and assert the result is Err with text containing '32 bytes'. Similarly, a 33-byte file should also be tested. This is a startup-failure safety invariant — if an operator accidentally provides a truncated key file the daemon must refuse to start with a clear error, not panic or use a wrong key. Without a test, a future refactor could silently remove the length check. Oracle: the error text 'must contain exactly 32 bytes' is the defined sentinel in the implementation.
